title: Introduce graceful quiesce/drain and shard-lease consistency for continuous batch coordinator
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem statement:
The continuous batching coordinator currently has a blunt shutdown/restart path that forces in-flight requests to either be retried at higher latency or dropped when a slot is migrated. We also observe stale KV cache reads during shard reassignments after scheduler churn, which leads to rare but high-severity token-level regressions for long-context sessions. This ticket refactors the coordinator to support a graceful quiesce/drain mode and introduces a lightweight shard-lease protocol to guarantee KV consistency across migrations while keeping throughput impact minimal.

Goals:
- Add a quiesce mode to the continuous batch coordinator so workers can finish inflight batches without accepting new work for a configurable window.
- Implement shard-lease metadata and a lease-renewal/handshake path to avoid stale KV reads during shard moves.
- Reduce lock contention in the scheduler hot path by switching a few critical data structures to lock-free read path (read-copy-update style) and materialize a small, versioned routing table.
- Provide metrics and tracing spans (quiesce_start, quiesce_drain_complete, lease_acquire, lease_release, lease_renew_fail) for SLO analysis and postmortems.
- Create a canary rollout plan to validate latency/cost regressions and KV correctness on low-traffic clusters before fleet-wide rollout.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Consistent hashing vs explicit shard leases: we prefer explicit shard leases to get deterministic ownership boundaries and simpler correctness reasoning during moves. Consistent hashing would reduce coordination but complicates strong KV invariants for cached prefixes.
- Synchronous lease handoff vs asynchronous reconciliation: use synchronous handshake on the critical path for small batches (to guarantee no stale reads) and allow background reconciliation for rare missed-acks to avoid blocking tokens.
- Quiesce window length: default 500ms with configuration per-instance; shorter windows reduce user-visible latency during scale-down but increase chance of in-flight split batches. We will capture latency distributions and allow ops to tune.
- Lock-free routing table: implement atomic pointer swap of a small immutable routing map to eliminate a mutex in the hot path. This is more complex but lowers contention under high QPS.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Define shard-lease protobuf and wire format; add lease table to coordinator with in-memory index and persistent event logged to the runtime journal.
2) Implement coordinator quiesce API: /internal/quiesce?duration_ms=... and integrate into autoscaler drain hooks and instance upgrade flow.
3) Add lease handshake in the placement/migration path: acquire-lease -> wait-for-inflight-drain -> release-old -> commit-lease. For speed, if the old owner acknowledges quickly, no blocking required.
4) Replace routing mutex with versioned routing map and atomic swap; keep mutex fallback for edge cases (e.g., huge routing updates).
5) Add unit/integration tests for lease correctness (simulate concurrent migration) and property tests for quiesce (no new accept while draining).
6) Instrument metrics and add tracing spans; wire to the Console per-route dashboards and add a short dashboard for rollout monitoring.
7) Canary rollout: start on dedicated staging cluster -> 10% fleet (non-critical customers) -> 50% -> full. Collect latency percentiles, tail latency, CPU/GPU utilization, cache hit rate, and KV consistency errors.

Testing & validation plan:
- Synthetic replay harness with long-context sessions to reproduce stale-read scenario and validate zero staleness after lease logic. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/kv-lease-test-harness
- Load tests comparing throughput/latency with quiesce enabled vs baseline; ensure p99 increase < 5% on steady-state workloads. Perf scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tests/perf/quiesce-bench
- Integration test asserting that during migration no token sequence returns content from wrong shard for >100k synthetic sessions.

Migration and rollout notes:
- Backwards compatibility: new lease metadata is additive. Older instances will ignore unknown lease fields but will not participate in lease-handshake; deployment should update control-plane first and then edge instances.
- Rollback: expose a feature-flag to disable quiesce/lease paths at runtime; rollback plan documented in PR.

Operational signals to watch post-deploy:
- Increase in request retries or 5xx during windowed rollouts (should be minimal).
- Lease_renew_fail rate > 0.1% indicates clock or connectivity issues.
- KV_cache_miss_rate change > 2x could indicate regression in caching behavior.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/Quiesce+and+Shard+Lease+Design
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5234
- Benchmark results (staging): https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/perf/quiesce-staging-2026-02-28

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want lease ownership to be multi-owner (for read-replica pattern) in the medium term? Currently single-writer single-reader model simplifies correctness.
- Should we persist lease events to the same runtime journal or a new compact lease log? Persisting to existing journal simplifies ops but increases journal size; a compact log reduces tail-read cost.

Acceptance criteria (done when):
- Quiesce API implemented and used in autoscaler drain flow.
- Shard-lease protocol implemented with unit and integration test coverage.
- No KV consistency regressions in the synthetic harness and staging canary.
- Dashboard showing lease metrics and rollout health.
- PR reviewed and approved by runtime owners and a short post-deploy runbook added to Confluence.

2026-03-07 - Ava Martinez: Addressed review comments, added integration test simulating 100 concurrent migrations; updated PR link. Perf run on staging looks acceptable (p99 baseline -> 4% increase under worst-case churn).
